meta.note: Visual reconstruction. Ancient/medieval distributions are hypothesis-driven and intended for continuity, not census-level precision.

events.title: Assyrian conquest of the northern kingdom
events.text: The northern Israelite population is disrupted while Judah remains the strongest surviving Levantine center.

events.title: Jerusalem destroyed; Babylonian exile
events.text: Part of the Judahite population is displaced eastward. A durable Mesopotamian Jewish center begins to emerge.

events.title: Hellenistic Jewish networks expand
events.text: Jewish communities become increasingly visible across Egypt, the eastern Mediterranean and major Hellenistic cities.

events.title: Second Temple destroyed
events.text: Jerusalem loses its central political role, while Galilee, Babylonia and Mediterranean diaspora centers remain important.

events.title: Distinct European traditions consolidate
events.text: Jewish life in the Rhineland, northern France, Italy and Iberia develops into increasingly distinct Ashkenazi and Sephardi cultural worlds.

events.title: Benjamin of Tudela describes a dispersed Jewish world
events.text: His itinerary records communities from Iberia through the Mediterranean to Mesopotamia, with Baghdad among the largest observed centers.

events.title: Expulsion from Spain
events.text: The Sephardi world fans out toward North Africa, Italy, the Ottoman Empire, the Netherlands and later the Atlantic world.

events.title: Wars devastate Polish–Lithuanian communities
events.text: The Khmelnytsky uprising and surrounding wars kill and displace many Jews, but Eastern Europe remains the fastest-growing Ashkenazi center.

events.title: First Partition of Poland
events.text: Large Jewish populations pass under Russian, Prussian and Habsburg rule, setting the stage for the later geography of the Pale of Settlement.

events.title: Pale of Settlement begins to take shape
events.text: The Russian Empire restricts most Jewish residence to its western borderlands, locking millions into a dense corridor from Lithuania to Ukraine.

events.title: Third Partition of Poland
events.text: The old Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth disappears; much of its Jewish population is now inside the Russian Empire and Habsburg Galicia.

events.title: Mass emigration from Eastern Europe accelerates
events.text: Pogroms, restrictions and economic pressure push millions toward the United States, Britain, Western Europe and Palestine over the following decades.

events.title: Russian imperial census captures the Pale
events.text: The Jewish population of the Pale is enormous and highly urbanized, but also distributed through hundreds of towns and shtetls.

events.title: Kishinev pogrom
events.text: Violence in Kishinev becomes an international symbol of Jewish insecurity in the Russian Empire and strengthens emigration and Zionist currents.

events.title: Legal restrictions of the Pale collapse
events.text: Revolution removes the old residence restrictions; Soviet urbanization later shifts large Jewish populations toward Moscow, Leningrad, Kyiv and other cities.

events.title: Prewar demographic peak
events.text: World Jewry reaches roughly 16.5 million. Eastern and Central Europe still contain the largest dense concentration of Jewish communities.

events.title: Holocaust annihilation accelerates
events.text: The dot cloud over Europe contracts rapidly as Jewish communities are deported, murdered and destroyed.

events.title: Europe's historic Jewish center has been shattered
events.text: Roughly six million Jews have been murdered. The world population has fallen by about one third from its 1939 peak.

events.title: State of Israel established
events.text: A new demographic pole forms. European survivors and Jews from the Middle East and North Africa increasingly converge in Israel.

events.title: Mass immigration reshapes Israel
events.text: Large migrations from Iraq, Yemen, North Africa, Eastern Europe and displaced-persons camps make Israel visibly multi-origin within only a few years.

events.title: Soviet Jewish emigration becomes a global issue
events.text: Restrictions remain tight, but pressure for emigration and Jewish cultural rights grows inside and outside the USSR.

events.title: Soviet Jewish emigration rises
events.text: Tens of thousands begin leaving the USSR, mainly for Israel and later also for the United States and other destinations.

events.title: Operation Moses
events.text: Thousands of Ethiopian Jews are airlifted to Israel, bringing Beta Israel into the same converging demographic story.

events.title: Soviet exit restrictions collapse
events.text: The largest late-20th-century Jewish migration begins. The former USSR rapidly loses population to Israel, the United States and Germany.

events.title: USSR dissolves; migration continues at scale
events.text: Israel receives hundreds of thousands of immigrants from the former Soviet Union while sizable communities also form in North America and Germany.

events.title: The Jewish world is concentrated in two poles
events.text: Israel and North America dominate numerically, but their populations contain layers of Ashkenazi, Sephardi, Mizrahi, Yemenite, Ethiopian, Persian and former-Soviet origins.
